study: Gorard, Siddiqui & See 2015, Philosophy for Children (P4C/SAPERE), EEF
eval_evidence: EEF-funded trial with Durham University as the independent evaluator; delivery org (SAPERE) was separate from the evaluation team.
developer_evidence: P4C training and ongoing in-school support delivered by SAPERE (the program's owning society/developer) via SAPERE-accredited trainers using standardised SAPERE methods.
cascade_evidence: SAPERE-accredited trainers trained the teachers directly and provided in-school support; no separate train-the-trainer intermediary between SAPERE and the participating teachers.
counterfactual_evidence: Waitlist control schools continued regular lessons / business as usual during the trial year (received P4C later).
coaching_evidence: Beyond 2 days' initial training, ~9 in-school support days over two years: trainers demonstrated P4C with children, helped plan lessons and gave feedback; periodic, not monthly+ recurring cycles.
student_dose_evidence: P4C delivered as ~1 enquiry lesson/week by the pupils' own teachers within regular timetable (changed instruction), not an added tutoring/pull-out/extra-minutes dose.
maturity_evidence: The measured KS2 cohort was exposed to P4C for 'just under a year' (single year of exposure for those pupils/teachers).
